text:
alex: Quick design question — proposing we route customer telemetry into per-tenant namespaces in the OTLP collector, then export to separate BigQuery datasets (or s3 prefixes) per tenant. Reason: isolation for PII/SLA and easier per-tenant retention. Thoughts?

maya: +1 on isolation for compliance. main risks are cardinality explosion and query ops cost. have we measured estimate for creating ~200 datasets? :thinking_face:

alex: good call. I ran a rough projection: storing raw spans per-tenant increases metadata but we can apply sampling + span aggregation per route before export. numbers: at current qps, full raw -> ~15 TB/month, with 10x sampling + aggregate -> ~1.5 TB. still TBD for 200 tenants distribution.

sam: curious how routing will work — do you plan to use resource attributes (service.name, tenant_id) in the collector pipeline? also how do we enforce RBAC so users can't query cross-tenant datasets?

jin: we can tag spans with `tenant_id` attribute and use the `attributesprocessor` in the collector to route to different exporters. config example:```yaml
receivers: [otlp]
processors: [batch, attributes]
exporters: [bigquery/tenant-123]
service:
  pipelines:
    traces:
      receivers: [otlp]
      processors: [attributes, batch]
      exporters: [bigquery/tenant-123]
```
then use a routing processor with `match` on attributes.

maya: that config snippet helps. what about dynamically provisioning exporters for new tenants? we can't maintain one static exporter per tenant in YAML for large scale. need a controller that updates collector config or a routing layer that writes to a central sink and a downstream job splits into tenant datasets.

alex: exactly — two options: 1) dynamic collector config (k8s controller that PATCHes collector configmap per tenant) or 2) central sharded export (collector writes to Kafka/S3 partitioned by tenant, then async job writes to BigQuery per tenant). Option 2 scales better but adds complexity/lag.

sam: for RBAC, BigQuery dataset-level IAM is straightforward if we have per-tenant datasets. If we use a central bucket with prefixes, we'll need object-level ACLs or a gateway that enforces access. dataset-per-tenant gives clean RBAC and simplifies audit logs.

maya: retention policies are important too. product wants 90d by default, but enterprise customers ask for 13 months. We need per-tenant retention config that the export path respects. Can't rely on BigQuery table TTL alone if we batch into multi-tenant tables.

jin: proposal: exporters write to intermediate tenant topics with metadata including retention TTL. a downstream worker materializes into per-tenant BigQuery tables with table-level expiration set. That lets us support different retention per tenant without collector reconfig.

alex: tradeoffs: latency (stream -> materializer adds ~5-15s), operational overhead (more components), and cost (extra storage/transfers). but we get per-tenant billing and RBAC.

maya: also watch cardinality: many tenants -> more partitions -> increased query planning overhead. for dashboards we should offer a multi-tenant aggregated view (platform admins) and a tenant-scoped view for customers. need RBAC in console too.

sam: question about spans vs metrics/events: do we want to export all traces? maybe keep traces sampled heavily and export full metrics/otel logs to per-tenant stores. traces are the biggest cost.

alex: yes sampling policy: keep 100% for enterprise flagged tenants (small subset), 1-5% for others + tail-sampling for errors. we'll implement deterministic sampling in the collector plus a tail-sampler for traces with error status.

jin: one more: observability-bot: "Heads-up: prototype materializer job pushed to staging. Route: otlp -> kafka(tenant_key) -> materializer -> bq. Metrics available on /metrics. Deployment at 1763467905."

maya: :eyes: i'll run load tests on staging tomorrow to measure lag and cost. can you add a flag to enable/disable per-tenant export so we can A/B test?

alex: yes will add `export.per_tenant.enabled` feature flag to the deployment config. aiming for canary rollout next week.

sam: also add a catalog of tenant datasets to the console (owner, retention, region, IAM bindings) so support can quickly verify.

alex: noted — will add to console backlog. thanks all, next step: jin to finish materializer prototype, maya to perf test, sam to draft RBAC/IAM runbook. :thumbsup:
